scheme_name: D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme
description:
The D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to promote research in the field of social sciences and humanities. 

The scheme was established in the year 2017. 

It is named after the renowned Indian mathematician and statistician Dr. D. D. Kosambi. 

The primary objective of the fellowship is to encourage scholars to engage in research that contributes to the understanding of Indian society and culture. 

The fellowship aims to support innovative research projects that can lead to significant academic contributions. 

The scheme specifically targets young researchers and scholars who have completed their doctoral degrees. 

The fellowship provides financial assistance to selected candidates to facilitate their research activities. 

The total amount of the fellowship is INR 50,000 per month. 

The fellowship duration is for a period of two years. 

Selected fellows will also receive a research grant of up to INR 1,00,000. 

This grant can be utilized for research-related expenses such as travel, data collection, and other necessary resources. 

The eligibility criteria for the D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme are clearly defined. 

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. degree in social sciences or humanities. 

Candidates should be below the age of 40 years at the time of application. 

There is no specific income limit set for applicants. 

However, preference is given to candidates from underrepresented groups and those who have faced socio-economic disadvantages. 

The application process is structured and requires several steps to be followed. 

Interested candidates must submit their applications online through the official website of the Ministry of Culture. 

The application form must be filled out with accurate personal and academic details. 

Candidates are required to submit a detailed research proposal along with their application. 

The research proposal should outline the objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes of the proposed research. 

Additionally, applicants must provide copies of their academic certificates and a curriculum vitae. 

The deadline for submitting applications is usually set for the end of March each year. 

Applications received after the deadline are not considered for the fellowship. 

Once the applications are submitted, they undergo a rigorous evaluation process. 

A committee of experts reviews the proposals based on their academic merit and relevance to Indian society. 

Shortlisted candidates may be called for an interview to discuss their research proposals in detail. 

The final selection is announced in the month of June each year. 

Selected fellows are expected to commence their research work by July. 

The fellowship amount is disbursed monthly to the fellows' bank accounts. 

The research grant is provided in a lump sum at the beginning of the fellowship period. 

Fellows are required to submit progress reports every six months. 

These reports must detail the work completed and any challenges faced during the research process. 

At the end of the fellowship period, a final report must be submitted. 

This report should summarize the research findings and their implications for society. 

The D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. 

The Ministry of Culture is responsible for promoting arts and culture in India. 

For any inquiries regarding the fellowship, candidates can contact the Ministry of Culture directly. 

The contact details are available on the official website of the Ministry. 

The scheme has been well-received by the academic community. 

It has encouraged many young researchers to pursue innovative studies in social sciences and humanities. 

The fellowship has also contributed to the body of knowledge related to Indian culture and society. 

Since its inception, several fellows have successfully completed their research projects. 

Many of these projects have been published in reputed academic journals. 

The scheme has also fostered collaborations between researchers and academic institutions. 

It has created a platform for young scholars to share their findings with a broader audience. 

The D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme aligns with the Government of India's vision to promote research and innovation. 

It supports the national goal of enhancing the quality of higher education in India. 

The fellowship not only provides financial support but also encourages intellectual growth among young researchers. 

It aims to create a new generation of scholars who can contribute to the understanding of complex social issues. 

The scheme is a significant step towards recognizing the importance of research in the humanities and social sciences. 

It highlights the government's commitment to fostering academic excellence in these fields. 

The D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme is an example of targeted support for research that addresses contemporary issues in Indian society. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to empower scholars to explore diverse topics that can lead to social change. 

The fellowship is a valuable opportunity for young researchers to gain recognition and advance their academic careers. 

Overall, the D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme represents a crucial investment in the future of research in India. 

It provides the necessary resources and support to nurture talent in the humanities and social sciences. 

The scheme continues to evolve and adapt to the changing needs of researchers in these fields. 

As the fellowship progresses, it is expected to have a lasting impact on the academic landscape of India. 

This initiative is a testament to the importance of research in understanding and addressing societal challenges. 

The D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme is a vital component of India's commitment to fostering a robust research culture. 

It plays a pivotal role in shaping the future of social science research in the country. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a vibrant ecosystem for academic inquiry and exploration. 

The fellowship is not just a financial grant but a recognition of the potential of young scholars. 

It encourages them to delve into research that can inform policy and contribute to societal development. 

In conclusion, the D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme is a comprehensive initiative that supports young researchers in India. 

It provides the necessary financial assistance and resources to facilitate meaningful research in social sciences and humanities. 

This scheme is a significant step towards enhancing the quality and impact of research in these critical fields.
